summary: Anna Morpurgo Davies (1937–2014) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. She studied at Sapienza University of Rome (~1955–1959) and held a post at the University of Oxford from approximately 1964 to 2004.

Anna Sawerthal is a Tibetologist who earned an MA at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes and Johanna Buß. She completed her PhD at Heidelberg University, supervised by Birgit Kellner and Roland Wenzlhuemer, and also studied under Dawa Tsering and Norbu Tashi.

Anna Seidel (1938–1991) worked in Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Munich, University of Hamburg, and under Maxime Kaltenmark and Rolf A. Stein, later holding posts at École Française d'Extrême-Orient and Institut du Hōbōgirin (~1969–1991).

Anna Szabolcsi is a linguist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University and earned her PhD from the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, where she was a fellow (~1976–1989). She later held professorships at UCLA (~1990–1998) and New York University (~1998).

Anna-Pya Sjödin works in Indology and philosophy. She earned her PhD at Uppsala University (completed by 2007), where her doctoral supervisors included Gunilla Gren-Eklund, Eli Franco, Jonardon Ganeri, K. Venugopalan, and Toshihiro Wada.

Anne C. Klein works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She studied at Binghamton, Wisconsin-Madison, and Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, among other traditional teachers, later becoming Professor and Chair of Religious Studies at Rice University (~1987) and founding Dawn Mountain.

Anne Casile is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under Claudine Bautze-Picron. She held posts at the British Museum (~2008–2010) and the French National Research Institute for Sustainable Development.

Anne E. Monius (1964–2019) was a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies who earned degrees at Harvard under Diana L. Eck and Kausalya Hart. She taught at the University of Virginia (1997–2002) and Harvard University (2002).

Anne Feldhaus is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Manhattanville College (~1967–1971) and earned her doctorate at the University of Pennsylvania (~1971–1976). In 1981, she joined Arizona State University as a professor of religious studies.

Anne Hardgrove is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Carleton College (~1987–1991) and the University of Michigan (~1993–1999) before holding posts at the University of Texas at San Antonio in 2000 and ~2001.

Anne M. Blackburn is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies who completed graduate studies at the University of Chicago (~1990–1996). She served as Assistant Professor of Religion at Cornell University (~2001–2006).

Anne MacDonald works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She studied at the University of British Columbia under Shotaro Iida and under Lambert Schmithausen and Karin Preisendanz, later holding posts at the University of Vienna (attested 2008) and Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2012).

Anne Nishimura Morse works in Japanology and history/archaeology. She earned her PhD from Harvard University under John M. Rosenfield and Yutaka Hirata, later holding posts at Smith College (1988–1989), Tokyo National Research Institute (1988), Nara National Museum (1996), and Kyoto National Museum (1998).

Anne Ruth Hansen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history/archaeology who studied under Charles Hallisey. She held an attested post at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee in 2007.
Anne-Marie Blondeau is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Rolf A. Stein and held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études.
Annegret Bollée (1937–2021) was a linguist who studied at the University of Hamburg (~1957–1960), Aix-Marseille University, and the University of Bonn (1969).

Annemarie Schimmel (1922–2003) was a religious studies scholar who earned degrees at Humboldt University and the University of Marburg under Friedrich Heiler. She held professorships at Marburg, Ankara University (1954–1967), and Harvard University (1967–1992).

Annemarie von Gabain (1901–1993) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Sinology. She studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1923–1930), holding posts there (~1935–1945) and later serving as a professor at the University of Hamburg (~1957–1966).

Annette Baier (1929–2012) was a philosopher who earned degrees from the University of Otago (~1948–1953) and a PhD from Somerville College, Oxford (1952). She held posts at Carnegie Mellon University (~1968–1973) and the University of Pittsburgh (~1973–1995).

Annette L. Heitmann specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1987–1989), under David Seyfort Ruegg and Christian Lindtner, and earned a doctoral degree at the University of Vienna by 2002.
